No.1186 of 2006, whereby the learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 1,55,000/- along with Vinodbhai Ishwarbhai Bhoi vs Yakubhai Hussainbhai Khalifa on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97751563/

2.

The succinct facts leading to file the present appeal are that on 23.09.2006 at about 3:00 p.m.,
the wife of claimant no.1 and mother of claimant nos.2, 3 and 4-the appellants herein went to sell the Singhoda at village Dhanap Patiya situated on Himatnagar-Ahmedabad Highway Road and while she was waiting on the road for a vehicle to go to other village to sell Singhoda, in the meantime, the driver of jeep (respondent no.1 herein) bearing registration no.GJ-9-X-3663 came driving the jeep in very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and thereby, lost the control over the steering and hit Kanchanben because of which, the Kanchanben sustained grievous injuries on head and other parts of the body and during the treatment at Civil Hospital, Gandhinagar, succumbed to the injuries.
At the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 50 years and she was earning Rs.3,500/- per month by doing the business.
3. On being served, the insurance company had filed the written statement at Exh.17, thereby denying all the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for rejection of the claim.

4. Having considered the pleadings of the parties, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues at Exh.18:-
(1) Whether it is proved by the claimants that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving on the part of involved vehicle No.GJ-9-X-3663?
(2) Whether it is proved by the claimants that deceased succumbed to death due to the injuries sustained in the accident by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2220/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined involved vehicle?

5. In order to prove their claims, the claimants/appellants have led the following oral as well as documentary evidences:-
 Sr. no.

Particulars   
 Oral Evidence Evidence by way of Examination-in-chief of Mr. Vinodbhai Ishwarbhai Bhoi Documentary evidences Copy of inquest panchnama of deceased Kanchanben 4.
Copy of panchnama of involved vehicle jeep 23 6. Copy of insurance policy of involved vehicle jeep 25 6.
Having considered the material on record, the learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,55,000/- as a compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
The learned Tribunal has also dismissed the claim petition against respondent no.3-insurance company herein.

7. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the quantum of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2220/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal and the exoneration of insurance company-respondent no.3 herein, the original claimants/appellants preferred the present appeal.

8. Heard learned counsels for the parties.
9.

Mr. Hiren M. Modi, learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed serious illegality in exonerating the insurance company on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding the valid driving license.
He further submitted that the learned Tribunal had shifted the burden to prove the defense of the insurance company upon the claimants.

He further submitted that the learned Tribunal held that "in the present case, the petitioners have not produced the driving license of opponent no.1-driver of the involved jeep no.GJ-9-X-3663, therefore, the opponent no.1-driver of the involved jeep was driving the said jeep without driving license and dashed to the deceased-Kanchanben."

Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submitted that it is the defense of the insurance company that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding the driving license but no evidence was led by the insurance company to prove its defense.
However, the learned Tribunal had shifted the burden to prove this fact upon the claimants.
He further submitted that the finding returned by the learned Vinodbhai Ishwarbhai Bhoi vs Yakubhai Hussainbhai Khalifa on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97751563/

sentences.text: 3 Tribunal on that point is not sustainable.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that at the time of accident,
the deceased-Kanchanben was doing the business of selling fruits and vegetables and thereby she was earning Rs.3,000/-
per month but the claimants/appellants could not prove the income on record.

Therefore, the learned Tribunal has determined the income of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2220/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined the deceased as Rs.1,500/- per month, which is less than even the minimum wages, as notified by the State Government at the relevant point of time.
He further submitted that the accident took place on 23.09.2006, at that time, the minimum wages for the skilled worker was Rs.2,500/- per month.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal could have considered the income of the deceased atleast as Rs.2,500/- per month.
He further submitted that the learned Tribunal has also not considered the future prospects of the deceased-Kanchanben.
He further submitted even, the learned Tribunal has awarded a very meagre amount under the heads of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.

He further submitted that the compensation awarded under these heads must be enhanced in accordance to the ratio of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Versus Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and Ors., reported in 2018 (18) SCC 130.

sentences.text: He further submitted that the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified suitably and the present appeal is required to be allowed.

11. On the other hand, Ms. Kirti S. Pathak, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent no.3-insurance company, vehemently submitted that the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in holding that the insurance company is not liable to pay the awarded amount, as the respondent no.1-driver of the offending vehicle was not holding the valid license to drive the jeep in question.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition against the respondent no.3-insurance company.

So far as the quantum is concerned, the learned counsel for respondent number 3, vehemently NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2220/2010 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/10/2025 undefined
submitted that the learned Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased as Rs.1,500/- per month at the time of accident, as the claimants could not prove the income on record.
She further submitted that the learned Tribunal has awarded reasonable amounts under the heads of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.
Therefore, there is no infirmity in the impugned judgment and award and therefore, the present appeal deserves rejection.

12. Having considered the submissions of the learned counsels for the parties and having gone through the record, it is to be noted that the claim petition was filed by the husband and three children of deceased- Kanchanben on account of the death of the wife of appellant no.1 and mother of appellant nos.2, 3 and 4.
It is not in dispute that at the time of accident, the deceased was doing the business of selling fruits and vegetables.
It is also not in dispute that at the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 50 to 55 years.
Even the factum of accident and manner of accident have also not been disputed.
The insurance company raised the issue of driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Considering the defense of the insurance company, the learned Tribunal came to Vinodbhai Ishwarbhai Bhoi vs Yakubhai Hussainbhai Khalifa on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97751563/
4 the conclusion that the claimants could not prove that the driver of the offending vehicle was holding the valid legal driving license to drive the jeep in question at the time of accident.

entities.text: Vinodbhai Ishwarbhai Bhoi vs Yakubhai Hussainbhai Khalifa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is to be noted that it was the defense of the insurance company that the driver was not holding the valid legal driving license to drive the vehicle, but the insurance company neither examined its officer nor summoned any witness from the RTO office to prove this fact.

However, the learned Tribunal has wrongly shifted the burden to prove the defense of the insurance company on the claimants and held that the claimants could not prove that the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2220/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined legal driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
In my considered view, the finding returned by the learned Tribunal is not sustainable in the eyes of law, as the burden to prove the defense lies upon the insurance company and not on the claimants.
The insurance company neither led any oral nor any documentary evidence on record to prove its defence.
Therefore, the finding returned by the learned Tribunal on the point of driving license is not sustainable in absence of any evidence led by insurance company.
Therefore, the said finding is required to be interfered and accordingly, set aside.

13. At this juncture, it would be profitable to refer the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swaran Singh & Ors., reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under:-
"109(vi) Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving licence is/ are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swaran Singh & Ors., reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach" to allow defences available to the insured under Sec. 149(2) of the Act.]"

14. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Swaran Singh (supra), it would be just and proper if the insurance company is made liable at the first instance to pay the compensation to the claimants/appellants here, and thereafter, recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle i.e. NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2220/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined respondent nos.1 and 2.
15.
So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that at the time of accident, the deceased was doing the business of selling fruits and vegetables.
However, the claimants could not prove the income on record.

In the absence of proof of income on record, the learned Tribunal ascertained the income of the deceased at the time of accident as Rs. 1,500/- per month, which is lesser than the minimum wages as notified by the State Government at the relevant point of time.
It is also not in dispute that the accident occurred on 23.09.2006 and the minimum wages at that point of time was Rs.2,500/- per month for a skilled labour.

Thus, in the absence of proof of income on record, the learned Tribunal would have considered the minimum wages for determining the income of the deceased, but the learned Tribunal determined the income at lower Vinodbhai Ishwarbhai Bhoi vs Yakubhai Hussainbhai Khalifa on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97751563/
5 side.

sentences.text: Therefore, the finding returned by the learned Tribunal deserves to be modified and accordingly, in view of the notification of the State Government, the notional income of the deceased is determined as Rs.2,500/- per month.
The learned Tribunal has not added any amount on account of future prospects of the deceased.
Therefore, 10% of the monthly income is added to the notional income of the deceased on account of future prospects of the deceased.
Therefore, the total monthly income would come to Rs.2,750/- per month.

It is not in dispute that the deceased left behind by her husband and three children, therefore, in view of judgment Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr., reported in AIR (2009) 6 SC 3104, 1/4th of the income is to be deducted on account of personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr., reported in AIR (2009) 6 SC 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though the learned Tribunal has not returned any finding on the personal expenses, but perusal of the calculation NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2220/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined transpires that the learned Tribunal has deducted 1/3rd of the income on account of the personal expenses of the deceased.
The deduction of 1/3rd of the income on account of personal expenses of the deceased is not in accordance to the ratio of the judgment of Sarla Verma (supra).
Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased is required to be deducted by 1/4th as per judgment of Sarla Verma (supra).
Therefore, after deducting 1/4th, the monthly income would come to Rs.2,062.5/-, which rounded to Rs. 2,063/-.
16. As the age of the deceased was between 50 to 55 years, therefore, as per judgment of Sarla Verma (supra), the multiplier of 11 is to be applied.

Therefore, the future loss of dependency would come to Rs.2,72,316/- i.e. (2063X12X11).
17.
The learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- for loss of estate, Rs.10,000/- for loss of consortium and Rs.3,000/- for funeral expenses.

The compensation awarded under these heads are also at very lower side and the same is also required to be modified in accordance to the ratio of the judgment of Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram (supra) and accordingly, sum of Rs.18,150/- is awarded under the head of loss of estate and a sum of Rs.18,150/- is awarded under the head of funeral expenses.

Therefore, all the legal representatives are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of consortium.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,93,600/- i.e. (48400X4) awarded under the head of loss of consortium.

Thus, the appellants shall be entitled for the following compensation under the following heads:-

After deducting the said amount, the appellants shall be entitled for additional compensation of Rs.3,47,216/-(5,02,216- 1,55,000).
The learned Tribunal has awarded the interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Therefore, the additional amount of compensation shall also carry the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

The insurance company shall deposit the entire awarded amount including the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal and enhanced by this Court along with interest within the period of six weeks from today.
